steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Smart materials: change properties in response to stimuli — thermochromic (temperature), photochromic (light), shape-memory alloys (heat returns original shape). | Key Fact: Nanomaterials: engineered at 1–100 nm scale — graphene (200x stronger than steel, conductive, flexible), carbon nanotubes, nano-coatings. | Key Fact: Composites: two or more materials combined for superior properties — carbon fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP) for lightweight strength, fibreglass for boat hulls. | Key Fact: Hydrogel: water-absorbing polymer — used in contact lenses, wound dressings, agriculture (slow-release water), disposable nappies.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe how a shape-memory alloy works and give one practical application. | Explain why graphene is considered a 'wonder material' and discuss the barriers to its widespread use. | Compare a composite material with a single material for use in a bicycle frame.
